what: A single image floats on the display panel and fades out every 4 seconds over .7s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1). Once fully off, it switches to the next image and fades in on the same curve (it also fades in over .7s on first open). Clicking an image enters view mode: the rotation stops and data-viewer is set on the panel, where clicking the left half goes to the previous image and the right half to the next, instantly. Left and right arrow keys, a swipe over 50px and clicking a dot also switch instantly, and leaving with Esc or the close button resumes the 4-second rotation.

options.[data-fx-part=stage]: (If present) pressable image cell — if none, the whole attached element
options.[data-fx-part=title]: (If present) Slot for the current artwork name
options.[data-fx-part=dots]: (optional) slot where dot buttons are created, one per image
options.[data-fx-part=close]: (If any) Button that closes view mode
options.--fx-dot: Dot color of other images (.5 transparent), default --kf-accent

events.fx:change: When the image changes — detail { index, item }
events.fx:viewer: When opening and closing view mode — detail { open, index }

note: The original uses React state (4s setInterval → hide → next picture after 700ms → show again two frames later) and Tailwind transition-opacity duration-700 ease-in-out. The original locks body scroll in view mode, so in a one-screen panel the host page blocks the body. The display keeps cycling even off screen
